text: You can't claim to be anti-racist if you're not anti-capitalist, that's like being against a product but not being against the system that created and necessitated the outcome. For example, let's say you're against animal cruelty. However, all the products you buy are from makeup companies that test all their products on animals. It would be extremely hypocritical because you say you're against animal cruelty. However, without your funding and your support, animal cruelty will never cease to exist if you support companies that engage in animal cruelty. Guys, you often ask me how to improve your debating skills, your critical thinking, and your ability to come up with counterarguments. In my opinion, one of the best ways is to find controversial videos like this and try to pick them apart logically. Now, this lady says quite a lot of things in a relatively short video. And honestly, there are many different angles you could take here. But let's take it one step at a time. First, she says you can't claim to be anti-racist if you're not anti-capitalist. The first thing I notice is that this is an absolute statement. And absolute statements are usually among the easiest to challenge because you only need one valid counterexample to disprove them. So can we find someone who fought against racism but didn't oppose capitalism? How about Booker T. Washington, a prominent African-American leader who founded the National Business League in 1900, promoting black-owned businesses as a way to fight racial inequality? Or Floyd McKissick, who was a leader of the Congress of Racial Equality, fought against segregation, and later promoted something literally called black capitalism as a way to empower African-Americans? Are we seriously going to argue that these people weren't against racism because they didn't want to abolish capitalism? Now, you can disagree with their approaches, but disagreeing with someone's economic strategy doesn't automatically mean they weren't fighting racism. Then she says that's like being against a product but not being against the system that created and necessitated the outcome. Okay, so what exactly is she saying here? That capitalism created racism? That capitalism necessarily produces racism? Or that racism cannot exist without capitalism? Because these are different claims. We know that ethnic prejudice and ideas about the supposed inferiority of certain groups existed thousands of years before modern capitalism. So, clearly, racism doesn't require capitalism to exist. Now, does that mean capitalism cannot contribute to racism? Of course not. Capitalism can reinforce racial inequalities and businesses can profit from racial discrimination. But saying capitalism can contribute to racism is very different from saying capitalism necessarily produces racism. And if that's her argument, she actually needs to demonstrate it. Then she says, for example, let's say you are against animal cruelty. However, all the products you buy are from makeup companies that test all their products on animals. It would be extremely hypocritical because you say you are against animal cruelty. You know what? Fair point. If you are against animal cruelty, but you knowingly support companies that engage in it, I can understand why someone would call that hypocritical. But here's the problem. In her example, there's a clear connection between the company and the practice you are supposedly against. What she hasn't established is an equivalent connection between capitalism and racism. She's assuming that capitalism necessarily produces racism, but that's exactly what she needs to prove for her analogy to work. And there's another interesting angle. I assume she is anti-capitalist. Yet she is recording this video using products manufactured by private companies and uploading it to a privately owned platform. So, by her own logic, isn't she also supporting something she's supposedly against? Now, she could argue that participating in a capitalistic economy doesn't necessarily mean supporting capitalism as an ideology. And that's a reasonable distinction. But if that's her defense, shouldn't she also recognize that participating in a capitalistic economy doesn't necessarily mean supporting racism? Finally, she says, however, with your funding and your support, animal cruelty will never cease to exist if you support companies that engage in animal cruelty. Again, I understand the point. Supporting companies financially can help sustain practices you are against. But notice something. We started with a claim that you cannot be anti-racist without being anti-capitalist. And instead of proving that claim, she has spent the rest of her video discussing animal testing. The analogy might sound convincing, but it only works if the original connection between capitalism and racism has already been established. And again, that's precisely what she hasn't done. She could have argued that capitalism has historically reinforced certain form of racial inequality. That's a legitimate subject to debate. But she went much further, claiming that you cannot even call yourself anti-racist unless you oppose capitalism. And that's a much stronger statement requiring much stronger evidence. So, here's my advice if you want to improve your arguments. First, be careful with absolute statements. One valid counter-example can be enough to disprove them. Second, make sure you understand exactly what you are claiming. Don't confuse something being a possible cause with it being a necessary cause. Third, actually build an argument and find evidence that supports it. And only then, if you want to make your point easier to understand, use an analogy. Because an analogy can help explain your argument, it cannot substitute for one. And that, guys, is how you should approach videos like this. Don't just look for something you disagree with. Look at the actual logic, identify the assumptions, and ask whether the conclusion really follows from the premise.
